Pink Floyd - The Wall

  • It's one of the only albums I know of that is not only an album, but also a movie. The only other one I can think of off the top of my head that isn't a soundtrack is Tommy, and the concept behind The Wall is way more interesting than Tommy.

  • It has some of the band's best songs on it (Another Brick in the Wall Pt. 2, Comfortably Numb), and yet all of the other songs on the album are also fantastic.

  • It pushes boundaries. It is as long as it could possibly be in order to be released on the most popular medium at the time, having to cut songs to do so. It uses strange recording techniques and song structures, as well as having each song run into each other

  • There are so many subtleties that even after many listens, there are things to be picked up. My favorite example of this: During The Trial, after The Worm says the line "The way you made them suffer, your exquisite wife and mother, fills me with the urge to defecate!", a man in the background, presumably in the courtroom, yells "Go on judge! Shit on him!". It cracks me up every time now, but it took me a long time to notice.

  • It loops in the most fascinating way I've yet heard an album loop. It starts with "..we came in?" and ends with "Isn't this where..", so that when the album loops, you hear someone saying "Isn't this where we came in?"

I could go on, because I've been obsessed with this album recently, but I have to go home from work now.
